messages.subject: Re: count events with stochastic mapping
messages.body_plain:
Hi!  Once you have the master_table_cladogenetic_events, you should be able to just summarize that table in various routine R ways -- e.g.:

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/9847054/how-to-get-summary-statistics-by-group

...I think I do this in the script somewhere but I forget.  As previously mentioned stochastic mapping is "beta" and needs more checking, documentation, and example/accessory scripts, but the basic results look reasonable...

Nick

> > Hi!  Thanks for the question.
> >
> > Yes, it's even easier than Lagrange to get the probabilities of each ancestral state. E.g. if the result object is "res", they are stored in the listed elements in "res":
> >
> > names(res)
> >
> > E.g. the probabilities of each states at each node are in:
> >
> > res$ML_marginal_prob_each_state_at_branch_top_AT_node
> >
> > The probabilities of each state at each "corner" (branch bottom, representing the states instantaneously after cladogenesis splits) are in:
> >
> > res$ML_marginal_prob_each_state_at_branch_bottom_below_node
> >
> > These tables have:
> >
> > rows: tips, then root node, then internal nodes -- numbered as in the APE package defaults or the prt() function
> >
> > columns: states (each state is a geographic range, e.g. for 2 areas there are 4 states/ranges: null, A, B, or AB
> >
> > See e.g.: http://phylo.wikidot.com/example-biogeobears-scripts#node_numbering
> >
> > Note that these are the state probabilities under the global ML model. Lagrange does state probabilities slightly differently, by fixing each ancestral state at each node and re-optimizing the model parameters under each constraint. They are typically similar but there can be some differences. See Matzke 2014, Sys Bio.

messages.subject: Re: Get only total ML of the model
messages.subject_clean: Get only total ML of the model
messages.body_plain:
Hi!  Yeah the global likelihood is printed out for each run you do, and is available in res$total_likelihood (or something similar).  This is the case for normal unconstrained runs as well as for any constrained runs.

Lagrange's tradition is to do "local optimization", reporting the LnL each time after fixing each possible state at each possible node, and calculates state probabilities from that.  I discuss the different between that and "ancestral state probabilities under the global optimum ML model", which is the BioGeoBEARS default, in Matzke 2014...

Cheers!
Nick

messages.body_plain:
Answer to a question about the "Your tree has Y fossil tips older than 0.6 my!" warning.  This will come up if you have fossils in your tree.  Read from the bottom...

---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: XXX
Date: Thu, Feb 19, 2015 at 10:59 AM
Subject: Re: Explanation of error message?
To: Nick Matzke <mat...@nimbios.org>

Hi Nick,

Thanks for that. Actually, the analyses weren’t working properly, but I seem to have solved that now - I found another error message that I had overlooked the firs time around.

Of course, please post the issue - anything to help others with this.

Cheers,
XX

On 19 Feb 2015, at 15:11, Nick Matzke <mat...@nimbios.org> wrote:

> Hi XX!  Glad you're playing with things!  Given your data, you should ignore the warning.  It's just in there for people who either (a) put in an un-dated tree and don't realize that all the tips that don't match the age of the highest tip will be treated as fossils, or (b) people who have fossils very close to the present but not quite at the present (in which case they need to change the default fossils_older_than).
>
> Can I post an anonymized version of this to the BioGeoBEARS google group to help others?
>
> Cheers!
> Nick
>
>
>
> On Thu, Feb 19, 2015 at 8:39 AM, XX wrote:
> > Dear Nick,
> >
> > Hope all’s well.
> >
> > I’ve been playing around with my BioGeoBEARS analyses and now have 22 time slices! Anyway, I’m getting the following error message -
> >
> > 'WARNING: Your tree has 43 fossil tips older than 0.6 my!
> > Make sure that 'fossils_older_than' is set to capture all of the fossil tips in your tree!
> > (default: fossils_older_than=0.6)’
> >
> > Can you tell me what this means and what I should do about it? It looks like I should add ‘;fossils_older_than’ etc. to my script, but I am not sure where this should go and what value I should set it equal to. All my taxa are fossils, with only one of them having a stratigraphic range extending as far as 66 Mya, which is effectively time 0 in this analysis (all other taxa stop well short of this boundary).
> >
> > Any advice would be greatly appreciated.
> >
> > Cheers,
> > XX
> >
> >
